text: Session 2 begins — The Stonehill Inn, Phandalin, midday of the 1st of Mirtul, 1492 DR.
location: The Stonehill Inn, common room

text: Last time: you escorted Gundren Rockseeker's wagon to Phandalin only to learn he'd been ambushed on the Triboar Trail. You tracked the Cragmaw goblins to their ravine hideout, fought through the sentries, and pulled Sildar Hallwinter — bruised, half-starved, and grateful — out of their larder. Sildar confirmed the worst: Gundren and his map to Wave Echo Cave were carried off to Cragmaw Castle on the orders of a mysterious 'Black Spider.' Now it's midday at the Stonehill Inn. Stew is on the table, Sildar is nursing his swollen eye across from you, and Phandalin — with its Redbrand problem — hums quietly around you.
location: The Stonehill Inn, common room

text: Sildar sets down his spoon and lowers his voice, glancing once around the common room. 'Nobody has ever seen the Black Spider. That's the first thing you should understand. The goblins whisper the name like he might be listening.' He holds up a finger. 'What I know is this: he's a dark elf — a drow. His kind live deep underground and almost never come to the surface, so whatever brought him up here, it's worth a great deal to him. He doesn't fight his own battles. He pays goblins and worse to do it — the same goblins that grabbed Gundren.' He leans closer, his one good eye steady on you both. 'And what he wants is Gundren's map. It leads to Wave Echo Cave — a lost mine with something inside called the Forge of Spells. A magical forge, from an age when dwarves and gnomes made enchanted arms there. Whoever controls it could make weapons the like of which nobody has seen in five hundred years.' He sits back. 'So it's simple, really. A hidden villain, a stolen friend, and a race for a magic forge. We know where Gundren is — Cragmaw Castle. The Spider is the one piece of this I can't see. And that worries me.'
location: The Stonehill Inn, common room

text: Sildar shakes his head slowly. 'About the Spider himself? No. No face, no real name, no one who's met him and talked about it after. That's what makes him dangerous.' Then he taps the table, remembering something. 'But here's a thing worth knowing. Gundren didn't find Wave Echo Cave alone. His two brothers — Nundro and Tharden — found it with him. Last Gundren told me, they were camped out near the cave entrance, guarding it while he fetched supplies.' His jaw tightens. 'The goblins took Gundren and his map. If the Spider finds that camp before we do... those two dwarves are sitting out there alone, and they don't know anyone is hunting them.'
location: The Stonehill Inn, common room

text: Sildar gives a grim little laugh. 'That's the rub. Nobody knows where the cave is. It stayed lost for five hundred years because it's that well hidden — somewhere in the hills east of here, and that's all anyone can say. Gundren knew the way. The map knows the way. And right now the goblins have both.' He counts on his fingers. 'So the road runs through Cragmaw Castle. Rescue Gundren, take back that map, and the cave is ours to reach first — brothers, forge and all. Fail, and the Spider gets everything.' He leans back. 'I don't know where the castle sits yet either — the goblins keep it hidden. Give me a day here and I'll shake its location out of my contacts. Or, if you can find a goblin willing to talk, they could point the way faster. You did let one walk out of that hideout alive, as I recall.'
location: The Stonehill Inn, common room

text: Relthus & Mira: "Do you know anything else about him?"
location: The Stonehill Inn, common room

text: Relthus & Mira: "Could we get to the cave to warn Gundren's brothers — and harness the power of the cave ourselves?"
location: The Stonehill Inn, common room

text: Relthus & Mira: "Let's track down that goblin. Relthus is an incredible tracker — and Yark owes us. If he double-crosses us, we can be... persuasive."
location: The Stonehill Inn, common room

text: The party leaves the Stonehill Inn and heads north out of Phandalin, toward the ravine country where they last saw Yark.
location: The Stonehill Inn, common room

text: Relthus finds the trail within the hour — small bare footprints in the soft ground by the stream, spaced quick and nervous. To his ranger's eye they tell a whole story: Yark left in a hurry, and he did not go home. The prints swing wide around the goblin hideout and cut northeast into the hills. The sun is dipping low when Relthus raises a fist: smoke. In a rocky gully below, a lone small figure crouches over a tiny fire, roasting something on a stick. Yark. His ears twitch — but he hasn't seen you yet. You have him: out in the open, alone, and upwind.
location: Rocky gully, Yark's camp

text: Relthus & Mira: "We approach slowly — no sneaking, no surprise. A hand on his shoulder: 'It's us. Mira and Relthus.'"
location: Rocky gully, Yark's camp

text: Yark shrieks, flings his dinner straight up into the air, and spins around with his hands raised — then sees who it is and sags like a puppet with cut strings. 'Ohhh. Ohh, it's the tall ones. The scary nice ones.' He catches the squirrel-on-a-stick as it comes back down, checks it for dirt, and clutches it to his chest. 'Yark thought you was Klarg's hunters. Klarg is ANGRY. Yark can't go back — dead sentries, empty larder, missing wolf... who gets blamed? Yark gets blamed.' His yellow eyes narrow, flicking from Mira's rapier to Relthus's bow, doing goblin arithmetic. 'You tracked Yark all the way here. Nobody tracks Yark for fun. What do the tall ones want?'
location: Rocky gully, Yark's camp

text: Relthus & Mira: "We want your help — do you know where Wave Echo Cave is, or anything about it?"
location: Rocky gully, Yark's camp

text: Yark's face scrunches up. 'Wave Echo... Cave?' He says it slowly, like the words taste strange. 'No. No no. Yark never heard of no echo cave. That's BOSS business. King Grol business. Spider business.' Then his ears perk, and a sly look crosses his face. 'Buuuut.' He holds up one grubby finger. 'The dwarf you keep asking about? The one the bosses grabbed? Yark knows where they TOOK him. Cragmaw Castle. Yark carried supply sacks there. Twice! Yark knows the paths, knows which way the guards look, knows the hungry tree to turn left at.' He hugs his squirrel stick tighter and looks up at them with big yellow eyes. 'Yark could show you. Yark WOULD show you. But Yark has no tribe now. Klarg wants Yark's ears in a bag.' He swallows. 'Take Yark with you. Feed Yark sometimes. And nobody puts Yark's ears in bags. Deal?'
location: Rocky gully, Yark's camp

text: Relthus & Mira: "Deal! Welcome to the party, Yark."
location: Rocky gully, Yark's camp

text: Yark blinks — once, twice — like he can't believe it worked. Then he leaps up and does a stomping little dance around the fire, waving the squirrel stick like a banner. 'DEAL! Yark has a tribe again! Best tribe! Tallest tribe!' He stops mid-stomp, suddenly serious, and points north where the last light is fading off the hills. 'Castle is two days' walk, through Neverwinter Wood. Dark now — bad time for walking, good time for squirrel.' He splits his dinner into three very unequal pieces and holds out the two biggest, beaming. 'Tribe eats together. Then sleep. Then Yark shows you the secret ways.'
location: Rocky gully, Yark's camp

text: Yark the goblin has joined the party!
location: Rocky gully, Yark's camp

text: Combat! Two of Klarg's goblin hunters burst from the dark at the camp's edge. Everyone is caught off guard — the goblins strike first.
location: Rocky gully, Yark's camp

text: Two arrows whip out of the darkness — one snaps past Relthus's ear, the other thuds into the bedroll a hand's width from Yark's head. Yark wakes screaming, 'KLARG'S HUNTERS! THEY WANT YARK'S EARS!' Two goblin shapes crouch at the gully's rim, silhouetted against the stars, already reaching for fresh arrows. Everyone is up now. Relthus moves first.
location: Rocky gully, Yark's camp

text: Relthus: "I shoot the goblin on the left with my longbow!"
location: Rocky gully, Yark's camp

text: Relthus draws and looses in one smooth motion. The arrow takes the left-hand goblin in the shoulder — it shrieks and staggers, clawing at the shaft, but stays on its feet, eyes burning with fury.
location: Rocky gully, Yark's camp

text: Yark, still tangled in his blanket, grabs his little bow and shoots back with a furious shriek — and his arrow slams into the right-hand goblin's chest. It topples backward off the gully rim without a sound. The last hunter looks at its fallen partner, looks at the arrow in its own shoulder, looks at three angry faces — and RUNS, scrambling up the slope and sprinting north into the dark, screaming for help.
location: Rocky gully, Yark's camp

text: Mira & Relthus: "Mira soothes Yark while Relthus chases the runner and shoots it from behind!"
location: Rocky gully, Yark's camp

text: Relthus vaults a boulder, tracks the fleeing shadow through the dark — breathes out — and looses. The runner tumbles into the rocks and doesn't get up. Silence returns to the hills. Back at the fire, Yark is shaking under Mira's arm, but her low, calm voice slowly works: 'They came for Yark's ears,' he whispers. 'Tribe protected Yark. GOOD tribe.' Nobody will carry word of you back to Klarg — or to the castle.
location: Rocky gully, Yark's camp

text: Combat over. Victory! +50 XP each — Relthus and Mira are at 250/300, close to Level 2.
location: Rocky gully, Yark's camp

text: Relthus & Mira: "We follow Yark north."
location: Rocky gully, Yark's camp

text: The party breaks camp at dawn and follows Yark north across the hills toward Neverwinter Wood.
location: Rocky gully, Yark's camp

text: The day's march is long but blessedly quiet. Yark trots ahead like a proud little scout, pointing out which berries are 'good eating' and which are 'dying berries, very bad.' Relthus hardly needs the help — by afternoon his snares and sharp eyes have gathered rabbit, wild onions, and enough berries to feed the whole tribe twice over. By evening, a dark green wall rises ahead of you: Neverwinter Wood, ancient and tangled, its canopy swallowing the last of the light. Yark stops at the tree line and lowers his voice for the first time all day. 'Castle is in there. One more day. From here... we go quiet. The wood belongs to the Cragmaws.'
location: Camp beneath the eaves of the wood

text: Relthus & Mira: "We camp and celebrate with camp food from Relthus's haul — s'mores, anyone? — and share the fun parts of the day."
location: Camp beneath the eaves of the wood

text: The fire crackles low and safe beneath the eaves of the wood. Dinner is a feast by trail standards: rabbit roasted with wild onions, and Mira's invention — hot mashed berries smooshed between two trail biscuits, which Yark declares 'the best food ever made by anyone, ever' with sticky purple fingers to prove it. The stories get bigger with every telling. By the third round, Yark's single arrow has slain ten hunters, and Relthus's shot in the dark was made blindfolded. Mira laughs so hard she nearly falls off her log. For one warm evening there is no Black Spider, no castle, no worry — just a small strange tribe under the stars, licking berry jam off their fingers. Morning comes soft and misty. The 3rd of Mirtul. The wood waits.
location: Camp beneath the eaves of the wood

text: Relthus & Mira: "We head into the forest."
location: Camp beneath the eaves of the wood

text: The party slips beneath the canopy of Neverwinter Wood, Yark leading along hidden game trails toward Cragmaw Castle.
location: Camp beneath the eaves of the wood

text: The wood is dim and green-lit, the mist never quite burning off. Around midday, Yark ducks under a fallen cedar — and freezes. Coming around the deadfall, thirty feet away, are two goblins in Cragmaw war paint with a gray wolf straining on a rope leash. Both groups stop dead. The wolf's hackles rise. One goblin's hand creeps toward its scimitar; the other squints at Yark, and its eyes go wide with recognition. 'Yark?' it hisses. 'Klarg says Yark is DEAD goblin walking. And look — Yark brought the tall ones that wrecked the hideout...' The wolf snarls. The rope creaks. Nobody has moved yet.
location: Camp beneath the eaves of the wood

text: Mira: (approaching the wolf slowly, palms open, voice low) "It's ok. We can protect you, and feed you good meals. We will take good care of you." Relthus, meanwhile, inconspicuously reaches for his bow.
location: Camp beneath the eaves of the wood

text: The wolf's snarl dies in its throat. Its ears swivel toward Mira's voice, and something in its eyes changes — it leans toward her, then PULLS, dragging the leash-goblin a stumbling step forward. 'Bad wolf! BAD—' The goblin looks up and finds the whole clearing has turned against it: the wolf straining toward the golden-haired human, the exile standing tall, the elf whose hand is somehow already full of bow. The goblin drops the rope like it's on fire. 'Not worth it. NOT WORTH IT!' Both goblins bolt north through the trees — toward the castle — shrieking as they go. The wolf doesn't even watch them leave. It pads to Mira, sits down at her feet with a whumpf, and looks up at her: well? You promised good meals.
location: Camp beneath the eaves of the wood

text: Relthus & Mira: "Relthus shoots the goblins before they can escape. Mira opens a packet of cooked rabbit for the wolf."
location: Camp beneath the eaves of the wood

text: Relthus's first arrow smacks into a cedar trunk. His second whistles through the gap where a goblin's head was half a heartbeat earlier — and then the trees swallow them both. Their shrieks fade north. The castle will hear about this. Behind him, blissfully unbothered, the wolf is inhaling cooked rabbit out of Mira's hand, tail thumping the forest floor like a drum. Yark watches the treeline, ears flat. 'They'll tell the castle bosses,' he mutters. 'Tall ones coming. Yark the traitor with them.' He looks at Mira, then at the wolf, and shrugs philosophically. 'On the other hand... new wolf. Good trade? Maybe good trade.'
location: Camp beneath the eaves of the wood

text: Mira: "I'll call her... Black Pearl."
location: Camp beneath the eaves of the wood

text: 'Black Pearl,' Mira says, and the wolf's ears swing around like she's always known it. Yark tries it out — 'Blackpearl. Black. Pearl.' — and nods gravely, as if a great ceremony has concluded. Pearl celebrates by shoving her whole face into the empty rabbit packet.
location: Camp beneath the eaves of the wood

text: Mira: (petting Black Pearl) "Eat as much bunny as you want, girl. Good girl."
location: Camp beneath the eaves of the wood

text: Black Pearl polishes off every last scrap of rabbit, licks the wrappings clean, and then licks Mira's hands for good measure — thorough, professional, leaving no evidence bunnies ever existed. When Mira scratches behind her ears, the big gray wolf leans her whole weight into it until they're both nearly tipping over. Her tail has not stopped once. Somewhere in the last hour, without any paperwork, Black Pearl has decided: this is her person now. Yark buries the empty packet under a rock, muttering that 'good tribes leave no smells for trackers.' Ranger and goblin exchange a look of genuine professional respect.
location: Camp beneath the eaves of the wood

text: Relthus & Mira: "Then we head off towards the castle together."
location: Camp beneath the eaves of the wood

text: The party — ranger, fighter, goblin, and wolf — turns north through Neverwinter Wood toward Cragmaw Castle.
location: Camp beneath the eaves of the wood

text: Relthus & Mira: "We'll reach the castle by dusk, take a short rest out of sight, then use Black Pearl's nose and Relthus's night vision for a sneak attack by night."
location: Camp beneath the eaves of the wood

text: By dusk you're close — Yark signals a stop in a hollow beneath a rock shelf, half a mile short of the castle. Through the trees, up on its hill, you catch your first glimpse: Cragmaw Castle, a broken crown of seven crumbling towers, firelight flickering in the arrow slits. Then Black Pearl's head snaps up, nose working. A low rumble builds in her chest. Relthus follows her gaze into the failing light and his elven eyes find them: three goblins with a hooded lantern, picking their way through the trees a hundred yards east, poking bushes with spears. Hunting. Hunting YOU — and utterly unaware they've already been found. Yark grins a small sharp grin. 'Castle sent hunters out,' he whispers. 'Means three less INSIDE the castle.'
location: Hollow beneath a rock shelf, ~half mile south of Cragmaw Castle

text: Mira: (petting Pearl) "Good girl." — The party waits for backs turned, then springs the ambush: Relthus from the trees with his longbow, Pearl at a throat from behind, Mira slashing in with her rapier.
location: Hollow beneath a rock shelf, ~half mile south of Cragmaw Castle

text: CRACK. A branch snaps under Pearl's paw — the goblins whirl, lantern light swinging wild through the trees. 'AMBUSH! THE TALL ONES!' Combat begins at the edge of the lantern glow!
location: Hollow beneath a rock shelf, ~half mile south of Cragmaw Castle

text: THE AMBUSH SO FAR — Yark's arrow from the bush went wide. Black Pearl hit like gray lightning: one goblin died before it could scream (22 to hit, 8 damage). Relthus put an arrow in a second goblin's shoulder (26 to hit, 5 damage — it's badly hurt). Then goblin courage failed completely: the wounded one is fleeing NORTH toward the castle, the unhurt one EAST into the woods. Mira is up — the runners are 50-60 feet out. She can dash after one, send Pearl to run one down, or call targets for Relthus.
location: Hollow beneath a rock shelf, ~half mile south of Cragmaw Castle

text: Mira: "Pearl — the wounded one, north! Take it down!" She sprints east after the other herself.
location: Hollow beneath a rock shelf, ~half mile south of Cragmaw Castle

text: Mira crashes east through the brush and the fleeing goblin snags itself in brambles (Mira's chase 16 vs its 7) — she's on it in twenty strides, rapier drawn, the goblin still tearing at the thorns. To the north, Black Pearl streaks after the wounded runner like gray lightning — but it jinks around a stump at the last second and her jaws snap shut on empty air (7 vs AC 15, miss). It's still running, wolf a hand's width behind, the castle's firelight showing through the trees ahead. Relthus is up: one shot at the north runner (~80 feet, 2 HP left) before it's gone.
location: Hollow beneath a rock shelf, ~half mile south of Cragmaw Castle

text: Relthus: "I take the shot."
location: Hollow beneath a rock shelf, ~half mile south of Cragmaw Castle

text: Goblin3 takes 10 damage (now -8 HP) — DOWN
location: Hollow beneath a rock shelf, ~half mile south of Cragmaw Castle

text: Relthus exhales and looses through eighty feet of dark forest. The arrow takes the wounded runner square between the shoulders mid-stride (24 to hit, 10 damage) — it tumbles into the leaves and lies still, fifty yards short of carrying its warning home. Pearl skids to a stop over it, sniffs once, and trots back looking mildly robbed. To the east, the last goblin rips free of the brambles, turns, and finds Mira's rapier point six inches from its nose. Its scimitar hits the dirt. Its hands shoot up. 'MERCY! Mercy mercy mercy! Grib surrenders! Grib was never even HERE!'
location: Hollow beneath a rock shelf, ~half mile south of Cragmaw Castle

text: ⚔ Combat over.
location: Hollow beneath a rock shelf, ~half mile south of Cragmaw Castle

text: Victory! Two hunters down, one prisoner — and nobody escaped to warn the castle. +75 XP each: Relthus and Mira hit 325 XP — LEVEL 2! Relthus unlocks ranger spellcasting; Mira gains Action Surge.
location: Hollow beneath a rock shelf, ~half mile south of Cragmaw Castle

text: Session 2 ends here — camped in the dark half a mile from Cragmaw Castle, level 2 waiting, and one very chatty prisoner. See you next time!
location: Hollow beneath a rock shelf, ~half mile south of Cragmaw Castle

text: Session 3 begins. Dusk, 3rd of Mirtul — a hollow beneath a rock shelf, half a mile south of Cragmaw Castle. Seven ruined towers stand against the darkening sky, firelight glowing in the arrow slits.
location: Hollow beneath a rock shelf, ~half mile south of Cragmaw Castle

text: Level 2! Relthus (HP 20) awakens his ranger magic — Cure Wounds and Ensnaring Strike. Mira (HP 17) gains Action Surge. Both stand 325/900 toward level 3.
location: Hollow beneath a rock shelf, ~half mile south of Cragmaw Castle

text:
Something wakes in Relthus as he sits watch beneath the rock shelf — the old language of the forest, suddenly answering when he listens. Green light flickers briefly between his fingers and is gone. Beside him Mira rolls her shoulders, and the tiredness of three days' march just isn't there anymore. You are stronger than the two travelers who left Phandalin.

Yark watches the green light with huge eyes. "Tall one does FOREST magic now," he whispers. "Yark's tribe is the BEST tribe." Grib, tied by the cold fire pit, looks considerably less delighted.
location: Hollow beneath a rock shelf, ~half mile south of Cragmaw Castle

text:
Mira unwraps a ration and lays it out for Black Pearl, cupping water in her hands from the waterskin. The wolf eats like she has never once been fed on purpose — then, when it's gone, presses her big head into Mira's shoulder and stays there. Something is decided in that moment, wolf-fashion, and it is permanent.

Across the camp, Relthus crouches in front of Grib and says nothing at all for a long moment — just sets one arrow down in the dirt between them, the way you'd set down a question. "Your friends didn't answer me," he says quietly. "You will."

Grib talks so fast he nearly bites his own tongue. "King Grol is boss! Big bugbear, VERY mean! Dwarf prisoner is in Grol's own room — Grol keeps the map there too, won't let ANYONE touch it! And — and there's a visitor! Messenger from the dark elf, come to BUY the map! Two dozen fighters in the castle, maybe more. And the tower — don't go in the tower with the smell! Owlbear lives there. It ate Zorp." He swallows. "Best way in is the broken wall, south-east side. Supply goblins use it. Yark knows it. Traitor Yark." He shoots Yark a look, then thinks better of it and stares at the dirt.
location: Hollow beneath a rock shelf, ~half mile south of Cragmaw Castle

text:
It is over quickly, and Relthus does not make a ceremony of it. The fire takes the rest. Yark stands very still through all of it, ears flat, and when Relthus shoulders his bow the little goblin falls in behind him without one single word — the chattiest creature in the North, silent as a stone.

You move through the dark trees toward the towers. Halfway there a dead branch cracks under Mira's boot like a snapped bone — everyone freezes — a torch drifts along an arrow slit, pauses... and moves on. Pearl presses flat to the ground beside Mira until the light is gone.

From the treeline, two hundred feet out, Relthus reads the castle the way other people read a page. Seven broken towers. Two goblin sentries in the gatehouse slits flanking the barred main gate — safe behind stone, poor targets. But on the rubble of the collapsed south-east wall, exactly where Yark said the supply path runs, a single goblin sentry sits nodding over his spear — a clean shot, wide open. A torch makes a slow round through the great hall, roughly every ten minutes. Near the gate, a strange saddled beast stands tethered — someone important is visiting. And from the tallest tower comes a smell of old meat, and once, a screech that is not any owl and not any bear.
location: Treeline vantage ~200 ft south of Cragmaw Castle

text:
Relthus draws in one long breath, lets half of it out, and looses. The arrow crosses two hundred feet of night in a heartbeat. On the rubble of the broken wall, the dozing sentry simply tips sideways behind the stones, spear still cradled in his arms, and does not get up. No cry. No alarm. The wind moves in the trees, the torch in the great hall makes its slow rounds, and the supply path into Cragmaw Castle stands open and unwatched.

Yark stares at the distant rubble, then at Relthus, and mouths — silently, faithfully — "best tribe."
location: Treeline vantage ~200 ft south of Cragmaw Castle

text:
Mira studies the tethered creature through the dark, the torchlight by the gate sketching its outline. Not a horse. A giant lizard — pale, blunt-snouted, claws made for climbing stone walls and cave ceilings. The kind of mount dark elves ride in the deep places under the world. Its saddlebags are still packed and buckled. Whoever rode it here isn't planning to stay long.

Meanwhile Relthus and Yark ghost across the open ground, low and quick, and fold into the shadow of the collapsed south-east wall. Up close the breach is a spill of broken stone with a worn footpath threading through it — the supply road Yark promised. The dead sentry lies where he fell behind the rubble. Beyond the gap: a dark, cold corridor into the castle, and somewhere down it, the smell of woodsmoke and roasting meat. Yark holds up fingers and points — this way to the kitchens, THAT way to the big hall. Nobody has raised any alarm.
location: Treeline vantage ~200 ft south of Cragmaw Castle

text:
Mira and Pearl come across the open ground like two more pieces of the night, and then the whole party is together in the shadow of the breach. Relthus kneels by the fallen sentry, works his arrow free, wipes it once, and slides it back into the quiver. Nine arrows.

Then, one by one, you climb through the broken wall into Cragmaw Castle. The supply corridor is narrow, cold, and dark — old stone, older dust, Yark's small hand tugging Relthus's sleeve at each turning. The smell of roasting meat grows stronger with every step, and now there's sound with it: the clatter of pots, and two goblin voices arguing furiously about — as best anyone can tell — soup. Firelight leaks under a crooked door ahead. The kitchen. From somewhere deeper in the castle, muffled through stone, comes a low boom of a big voice laughing, and many smaller voices laughing quickly after it, the way you laugh when the boss expects it.
location: Cragmaw Castle — supply corridor inside the collapsed SE wall, nearing the kitchen

text:
Relthus pushes the crooked kitchen door open one inch and looks through the gap. Everyone else waits in the dark hallway right behind him: Mira next, then Pearl the wolf, then Yark at the back.

Here is what Relthus sees inside the kitchen:

There are exactly two goblins, and they are cooks, not fighters. Both of them are on the FAR side of the room, standing at a cooking fire against the back wall, with their backs turned to the door. One is stirring a huge pot. The other is turning a roast on a spit, and they are still arguing about the soup. Neither one has heard anything.

In the middle of the room is a big wooden table covered in vegetables, knives, and dirty bowls. You could hide behind it.

On the RIGHT side of the kitchen there is a second door. The laughing and shouting of the goblin feast comes from behind that door — that is the way to the great hall, where King Grol is. The kitchen has no other people in it. Just the two cooks with their backs turned.

If you move now, quietly, you can cross the room and be right behind them before they ever know you're there.
location: Cragmaw Castle — supply corridor inside the collapsed SE wall, nearing the kitchen

text: Relthus (whispering): "Is there another way around? A way to Grol's room that doesn't go through the great hall?"
location: Cragmaw Castle — supply corridor inside the collapsed SE wall, nearing the kitchen

text:
Yark nods hard and points down the dark hallway, PAST the kitchen door, deeper along the castle wall.

He whispers: "Supply hall keeps going. Past kitchen is the storeroom — barrels, sacks, no goblins at night. Behind the storeroom is the old back passage. It goes behind the big hall, all the way to the back towers. King Grol sleeps in the far back tower. Yark carried his food there. Two times."

Then his ears droop and he holds up two fingers. "But the back passage goes past two bad places. It goes past the tower that smells like old meat — that is the owlbear's tower. The door to it is broken. And it goes past the old shrine room, where the goblins will not go at night. Something lives in there. Yark never saw it. Yark only heard it click."

So this is what you know now: the hallway you are standing in continues past the kitchen door to a storeroom, and behind the storeroom a back passage leads to King Grol's tower without going through the great hall — but that passage runs past the owlbear's broken door and past the shrine room with the clicking thing in it.
location: Cragmaw Castle — supply corridor inside the collapsed SE wall, nearing the kitchen

text:
You slip into the kitchen one at a time and spread out exactly as planned. Mira and Pearl creep up behind the goblin turning the roast. Relthus and Yark creep up behind the goblin stirring the pot. The cooks keep arguing about soup. They never once look back.

Relthus gives the signal.

It is over in one second. Mira's rapier and Relthus's shortsword strike at the same moment, and both cooks drop without a single sound — Pearl and Yark never even have to move. Relthus catches the roasting spit before it can clatter to the floor. The pot keeps bubbling. The fire keeps crackling. Behind the right-hand door, the feast in the great hall roars on, and nobody there knows anything happened.

The kitchen is yours. It is quiet except for the fire. The hallway you came from leads back out to the storeroom and the back passage. The door on the right leads to the great hall and the feast.
location: Cragmaw Castle — supply corridor inside the collapsed SE wall, nearing the kitchen

text: Session 3 ends here — a short one, but a clean one. The party holds the quiet kitchen of Cragmaw Castle: Relthus, Mira, Yark, and Black Pearl, unhurt and undiscovered, while King Grol's feast roars on one door away. Somewhere in the far tower, a dwarf and a map are waiting. See you next session.
location: Cragmaw Castle — kitchen (secured), off the SE supply corridor

text:
Session 4 begins. Early night, 3rd of Mirtul — inside Cragmaw Castle.

Here is where everyone is: Relthus, Mira, Yark, and Black Pearl are all together in the castle kitchen, which you took silently last session. The two cooks are dead. Nobody in the castle knows you are here.

Through the door on the RIGHT side of the kitchen, you can hear King Grol's feast — lots of goblins, one big booming voice. Somewhere in there is the dark elf's messenger, who came to buy the map to Wave Echo Cave. His riding lizard is still tied up outside with packed bags — he plans to leave soon.

The hallway you came in through leads to the storeroom, and behind that, the back passage to King Grol's tower — where Gundren the dwarf and the map are kept. The back way passes two dangers: the owlbear's tower with the broken door, and the shrine room where something clicks in the dark.

One more thing to remember: sooner or later, somebody at that feast is going to wonder where their food is.
location: Cragmaw Castle — kitchen (secured), off the SE supply corridor

text:
Mira eases the right-hand door open a finger's width and puts her eye to the crack. Nobody sees her — every face in the hall is turned toward the food and the throne.

Here is what she sees, one thing at a time:

The great hall is long, loud, and lit by two big fire pits. At the FAR end, on a throne of stacked stone, sits King Grol — a bugbear, which means a goblin the size of a bear, all shoulders and yellow fangs. A huge gray wolf lies at his feet. That must be Snarl.

Sitting beside the throne is the visitor: a slim figure in a dark hooded cloak, ash-gray hands, sipping from a cup and not eating anything. The dark elf's messenger. And on the table between the messenger and the king lies a leather tube — exactly the kind you carry a rolled-up MAP in. They are still talking. Whatever the deal is, it isn't finished.

Between Mira and the throne: about TWELVE goblins at the feast tables, eating, shouting, and paying attention to nothing. But by the big main doors at the far side stand TWO hobgoblins — bigger than goblins, in real armor, and they are not eating. They are guarding. Fifteen enemies in this room, all told, counting the king and the wolf and the messenger.
location: Cragmaw Castle — kitchen (secured), off the SE supply corridor

text:
You slip back out of the kitchen the way you came, down the dark supply hall, and through the next door: the storeroom. Yark was right — no goblins here at night. Just barrels, sacks, and dust, with the feast a distant rumble through the stone.

Searching quietly in the dark, here is what you find and take:

A bundle of TWENTY goblin arrows — Relthus's quiver is full again, 29 arrows now. SIX torches, which matter because Mira cannot see in the dark like Relthus and Yark can. A clay flask of lamp oil, the kind that burns. And two more days of food from the sacks.

One more thing: shoved in a corner is a wooden crate stamped with a BLUE LION — a merchant's mark, not a goblin thing. This was stolen from a trader. Inside are two short swords and a wooden shield. Good gear, but heavy and clattery — carrying it while sneaking would be a problem. You leave the crate where it is, and you know where to find it.

From the storeroom's back wall, a low doorway opens onto the old back passage Yark described — the one that leads behind the great hall toward King Grol's tower, past the owlbear and the shrine.
location: Cragmaw Castle — kitchen (secured), off the SE supply corridor

text:
The back passage is narrow and pitch dark — Relthus and Yark leading with their night eyes, Mira's hand on Relthus's shoulder, Pearl padding behind. Halfway along, you reach it: a splintered doorway on the left side of the passage, the door itself long since smashed to kindling. The smell rolling out of it is terrible — old meat and wet feathers. The owlbear's tower.

You start past it, slow as honey. And then a claw ticks on stone — too loud — and everything on the other side of that doorway goes silent. Listening.

Then it comes. Filling the broken doorway fifteen feet ahead of you: a monster the size of a cart-horse, with the body of a bear and the face of a giant owl, round yellow eyes glowing in the dark. Feathers bristle along its neck. It has heard you. It is looking RIGHT at you. Its beak opens.

Nobody in the castle will come running — the goblins are afraid of this thing and ignore its screams. But it stands between you and King Grol's tower, and it is very much awake.
location: Cragmaw Castle — storeroom off the supply hall, at the mouth of the back passage

text: ⚔ Combat! Initiative: Relthus (21) → Owlbear (20) → Mira (13) → Pearl (8) → Yark (3)

location: Cragmaw Castle — storeroom off the supply hall, at the mouth of the back passage

text:
The fight explodes in the narrow dark. Here is round one, blow by blow:

Relthus is fastest. His arrow leaps the fifteen feet and buries itself in the owlbear's shoulder — a solid, deep hit. The monster does not fall. It ROARS.

Then it charges Relthus. Its beak snaps shut an inch from his face — he jerks back just in time — but its claws catch him across the chest and slam him into the passage wall. Relthus is badly hurt now. One more hit like that would put him down.

Mira's torch flares to life and she swings it at the monster's face. It flinches from the fire — the flame scares it, that much is clear — but the swing doesn't land. Pearl darts around behind it and lunges for a leg, but her teeth close on a mouthful of feathers.

Yark presses himself flat against the wall in the shadows, eyes huge, not moving.

The owlbear stands wounded in the middle of the passage, arrow in its shoulder, torchlight dancing in its round yellow eyes. Round two. Relthus, you're up — you have 5 HP.
location: Cragmaw Castle — storeroom off the supply hall, at the mouth of the back passage

text:
Relthus looses his arrow with the monster's breath hot on his face — and the shot goes wrong, glancing off bone and shattering against the stone. The magic vines he had gathered around his bow hand flicker, waiting for a hit that doesn't come.

Then the owlbear's claws come down.

Relthus is thrown across the passage like a doll. He hits the wall and slides down it and DOES NOT GET UP. He is alive — barely — but he is unconscious on the stone floor, bleeding, and the owlbear is standing over him.

Mira is on her feet with a burning torch in her hand. Pearl is behind the monster, hackles up. Yark is frozen against the wall. The owlbear looms over Relthus's body, arrow still jutting from its shoulder.

Mira — it's your turn. Relthus is dying on the floor fifteen feet from you. What do you do?
location: Cragmaw Castle — storeroom off the supply hall, at the mouth of the back passage

text: Owlbear takes 8 damage (now 41 HP)
location: Cragmaw Castle — storeroom off the supply hall, at the mouth of the back passage

text: Owlbear takes 6 damage (now 35 HP)
location: Cragmaw Castle — storeroom off the supply hall, at the mouth of the back passage

text:
Mira answers the monster with steel and fire together. Her first thrust slips through feathers and bites deep — and then she does something fighters twice her age can't do: she surges, torch driving at the owlbear's eyes while her rapier darts in AGAIN under its beak. Two hits. The monster reels backward off of Relthus's body, half-blind and bleeding, and Pearl's jaws clamp onto its haunch from behind. It is hurt now — really hurt — though far from finished.

Yark scrambles out of the shadows to Relthus, pressing his small hands over the wounds, whispering "no no no, tall one, NO" — but there's too much blood and his hands are shaking too hard.

And then Relthus's eyes snap open on their own.

Call it the forest's old magic, call it a ranger's stubbornness — his heart simply refuses. He is awake, flat on his back on the cold stone, one breath away from death, with the owlbear looming right there above him in the torchlight.
location: Cragmaw Castle — storeroom off the supply hall, at the mouth of the back passage

text:
Relthus's blade glances off the monster's belly, and the owlbear answers.

The beak strikes down once. Then the claws. And this time the forest's old magic does not come. This time his eyes do not open.

Relthus — the quiet ranger who watched the tree lines, who tracked Yark through the gully, who put an arrow through the dark at two hundred feet — is gone. His bow lies beside his open hand. It happens the way it happens in the old stories: suddenly, unfairly, and forever.

Yark makes a sound no one has ever heard a goblin make.

The owlbear raises its head from the body, torchlight in its yellow eyes, blood on its beak. Mira is standing ten feet away with fire in one hand and steel in the other, and her friend is dead on the stone, and the monster that did it is looking at her now.

Mira. It's your turn.
location: Cragmaw Castle — storeroom off the supply hall, at the mouth of the back passage

text: TABLE RULING: We are rewinding one turn. Relthus's death is undone — the choice he made at 1 HP was based on unclear information in the chronicle (the owlbear's TWO separate attacks per turn were never made explicit). We resume from Relthus's turn: alive, awake, 1 HP, lying under the owlbear. He casts Cure Wounds on himself instead. All dice from here are rolled fresh and stand as they land.
location: Cragmaw Castle — storeroom off the supply hall, at the mouth of the back passage

text:
Flat on his back with the owlbear's shadow over him, Relthus slaps his palm against his own torn chest and growls the forest's old words. Green light floods between his fingers like sun through leaves. Wounds pull closed. It isn't everything — he is still badly hurt — but strength comes back into his arms, and he rolls up onto his feet, standing again, shortsword in hand. That was his last spell; the forest has given all it has tonight.

The owlbear rears back, screeching at the light — and now it strikes at the elf standing in front of it. Remember: an owlbear attacks TWICE each turn — once with its beak, once with its claws. Here comes the beak—
location: Cragmaw Castle — storeroom off the supply hall, at the mouth of the back passage

text:
The beak flashes faster than the healing light fades. It hits Relthus like a hammer and he goes down AGAIN — alive, but out cold on the stones, badly wounded. The green magic is spent and cannot save him twice.

The owlbear's second attack — the claws — does not go for the fallen elf. Pearl's teeth are still buried in its haunch, and the wolf is the pain it can reach. The great paw sweeps around at Black Pearl—
location: Cragmaw Castle — storeroom off the supply hall, at the mouth of the back passage

text:
—and the claws catch the wolf full in the side. Black Pearl is flung across the passage, hits the wall, and crumples. She is not dead — you can see her ribs rising and falling, fast and shallow — but she cannot get up, and she is bleeding. Like Relthus, she is running out of time.

So here is where things stand, all in one breath: Relthus is unconscious on the floor by the owlbear's feet. Pearl is unconscious by the wall. Yark is crouched in the shadows, unhurt. The owlbear is wounded — more than half its strength bled away by arrow, rapier, and fang — but it is still standing, still enormous, and there is fresh blood on its claws.

Mira is the only one left on her feet. Torch in one hand. Rapier in the other. Completely unhurt, with her fighting spirit (Second Wind) still unspent.

Mira. It's your turn. Everything is up to you.
location: Cragmaw Castle — storeroom off the supply hall, at the mouth of the back passage

text: Mira plants herself between the monster and her fallen friends, torch thrust forward so the fire fills its eyes. When it shies from the flame she drops low — gymnast-low — and her rapier flicks out and opens a red line across its front paw. The owlbear snatches the paw back with a screech, favoring it now. The wound is not deep, but the beast is slowing, bleeding from half a dozen cuts, and it has learned to fear the small human with the fire.

text: By the wall, Black Pearl's breathing steadies just a little — she is holding on. (That was a success on her first death save: one mark toward safe, none toward gone.)
location: Cragmaw Castle — storeroom off the supply hall, at the mouth of the back passage

text:
Yark tears a strip from his own ragged shirt, jams it against the worst wound, and knots it tight the way he's watched hunters do. The bleeding slows. Then stops. Relthus is still out cold — but he is no longer dying. Yark did it.

The little goblin looks up at Mira with huge wet eyes and whispers: "Yark held the tribe together. Now Mira makes the monster GO AWAY."
location: Cragmaw Castle — storeroom off the supply hall, at the mouth of the back passage

text: The beak stabs down at Mira — and she isn't there. She sways aside like a reed, the snap closing on empty air where her shoulder was. (A miss.) Now the claws—
location: Cragmaw Castle — storeroom off the supply hall, at the mouth of the back passage

text:
—and the claws meet the TORCH instead. Mira shoves the burning brand straight into the sweeping paw and the owlbear recoils with a screech, embers scattering across the stone. Both attacks, dodged or denied. The monster stands heaving in the passage, striped with wounds, one paw curled against its chest — and for the first time tonight, it takes a half-step BACKWARD, toward its broken doorway.

Mira's turn. She is still unhurt.
location: Cragmaw Castle — storeroom off the supply hall, at the mouth of the back passage

location: Cragmaw Castle — storeroom off the supply hall, at the mouth of the back passage

text: Torch in the eyes, blade in the ribs — Mira makes it one motion. The fire blinds; the rapier slides deep between the monster's ribs and comes back red. (A solid hit, 10 damage — the deepest wound anyone has dealt it.) The owlbear SCREAMS, a sound like tearing metal, and staggers sideways against the doorframe of its den. It is swaying now. Barely a quarter of its strength remains.
location: Cragmaw Castle — storeroom off the supply hall, at the mouth of the back passage

text: Pearl hangs on — her breathing evens out a little more. (Second death save: a success. One more and she's safe on her own.)
location: Cragmaw Castle — storeroom off the supply hall, at the mouth of the back passage

text:
Yark scrambles from Relthus to the wolf, pressing his hands over Pearl's wound, muttering "good wolf, GOOD wolf, stay." And it works — the bleeding stops. Pearl is stable too. Out cold, but safe. The little goblin has saved two lives tonight.

The owlbear, blinded by torchlight and bleeding from a dozen wounds, turns its bulk toward the broken doorway of its den — it is trying to RETREAT.
location: Cragmaw Castle — storeroom off the supply hall, at the mouth of the back passage

text:
Mira does not swing. Instead she steps back, lowers the torch, and opens the way to the den — her voice low and calm, the voice that won Black Pearl: "Go on. Go. Nobody has to hurt anymore tonight."

The owlbear stares at her, one paw curled to its chest, yellow eyes reflecting the flame. Something older than anger passes between them — hurt animal to animal-friend. Then it turns and drags itself through the broken doorway into its tower, feathers scraping stone, and is gone into the dark. You hear it settle somewhere deep inside, breathing hard, licking its wounds.

The passage falls quiet. The fight is over — nobody died tonight. Relthus and Pearl lie stable and sleeping, Yark kneeling between them, bloody to the elbows and grinning like he can't stop. Mira stands alone in the torchlight, without a scratch on her, in a castle that still doesn't know they're here.
location: Cragmaw Castle — storeroom off the supply hall, at the mouth of the back passage

text: ⚔ Combat over.
location: Cragmaw Castle — storeroom off the supply hall, at the mouth of the back passage

text:
Mira plants the torch in a crack in the stones, drags Relthus and Pearl close together against the wall, and stands guard over them in the dark hallway — rapier out, rations laid ready beside each sleeping head. Yark curls against Pearl's flank, one ear up.

The wait is long, and the castle does not stay quiet. Less than an hour in, a horn blows somewhere near the great hall — short, angry blasts. Shouting. Doors banging. THEY HAVE FOUND THE COOKS. Boots and torchlight go storming up and down distant corridors. Twice, light spills across the far mouth of your passage and goblin voices argue in whispers — "YOU look. Not Yark's old hall. The BIRD-BEAR is in there" — and twice, fear wins. No one comes in. The owlbear, for one night, is the best guard you could ask for.

Hours pass. The shouting dies down to tense, watchful quiet. And then, deep in the night, Relthus's eyes open. One point of health, aching everywhere, a ration and a waterskin waiting by his hand — and his friends' faces over him. Pearl still sleeps, breathing steadily, one hour from waking on her own.

Through the wall, faintly, you can hear the castle that is now wide awake and looking for you. Dawn — when the dark elf's messenger means to ride out with the map — is perhaps three hours away.
location: Cragmaw Castle — back passage outside the owlbear's den (post-fight; owlbear wounded, retreated inside)

text:
The party settles into the dark for one careful hour. Mira keeps watch with Yark; Relthus eats, drinks, rewraps Yark's bandages properly, and lets his body do its stubborn ranger work. The rolls are low — the wounds are deep — but strength comes back: Relthus rises to 11 of his 20 health. Both his hit dice are spent now; what he has is what he has until a real night's sleep.

As the hour turns, Black Pearl stirs, lifts her head, and thumps her tail once against the stone. Awake — barely, at the edge of her strength, but awake. She wobbles to Mira and leans on her, and eats the ration that was waiting.

The rest ends. The tally, plainly: Relthus 11/20, no spells left. Mira 17/17, fresh (her Second Wind recharged with the rest). Pearl on her feet at 1/11 — one hit from falling again. Yark unhurt. Two hours remain before first light, when the dark elf's messenger rides out with the map. The castle beyond the walls is quiet, awake, and hunting.
location: Cragmaw Castle — back passage outside the owlbear's den (post-fight; owlbear wounded, retreated inside)

text: ⚔ Combat over.
location: Cragmaw Castle — back passage outside the owlbear's den (post-fight; owlbear wounded, retreated inside)

text:
Mira kneels a moment with Pearl, forehead to furry brow — "you stay behind me, understand?" — and the wolf, for once, obeys. Then you move down the corridor in order: Relthus first, then Mira with the torch, then Yark, Pearl limping at the rear.

The corridor ends at a doorway with no door. Beyond it, your light and Relthus's night-eyes show you the shrine room: a round chamber, once holy, long ruined. A cracked stone altar stands in the middle under a partly fallen ceiling. Rubble is heaped along the walls. High in one corner, the roof is broken open to the night sky, and old bird nests crust the gap. The room smells wrong — sour, like a snake den.

And here is the thing you must know: the clicking has STOPPED. The room is completely silent. Relthus studies the rubble, the altar, the dark ceiling, for a long, careful minute — and cannot find what makes the sound. Whatever lives here, he cannot see it. But nothing has heard you either; the silence is the ordinary kind, not the listening kind.

On the far side of the round room, directly across from where you stand, the corridor continues — the last stretch to King Grol's tower. To cross, you walk through the shrine. About forty feet of open, rubble-strewn floor.
location: Cragmaw Castle — back passage outside the owlbear's den (post-fight; owlbear wounded, retreated inside)

text:
Relthus arcs the coin high across the round room. It strikes stone on the far side — TING, ting, ting-ting — and everyone flattens against the corridor wall outside the doorway, out of sight, holding their breath.

And the rubble MOVES.

Not the far rubble — the near heap, along the wall barely fifteen feet from the door, on your left as you'd enter. What you all took for a spill of broken masonry unwinds itself: a worm as thick as a barrel and longer than a rowboat, gray-green and glistening, with a snapping beak ringed by four whipping tentacles. Click. Click-click. That is the sound — its beak, tasting the air.

It pours across the shrine floor toward the fallen coin, silent as oil despite its size, and begins nosing through the rubble at the FAR end of the room — right beside the corridor that leads to Grol's tower.

So the trick worked, and now you know two things. You know what it is and where it is. And you know the path is clear on THIS side of the room — but the monster is now hunting exactly where you wanted to go.
location: Cragmaw Castle — back passage outside the owlbear's den (post-fight; owlbear wounded, retreated inside)

text:
Relthus watches the thing hunt, and an old campfire story surfaces — a tale traded between rangers about the deep caves. "Grick," he breathes. "Cave hunter. I've never seen one — but I've heard." Here is what the story says: it strikes from ambush with those four tentacles and drags prey to the beak. And the part every teller repeats — ORDINARY WEAPONS GLANCE OFF ITS HIDE. Swords, arrows, teeth — they bounce off that rubbery skin unless the blow is truly mighty. It's why the deep-cave folk just... go around them.

Yark tugs Relthus's sleeve and nods hard, whispering the goblin version: "Chief sent three warriors in there once. To clear the old shrine. Swords went bonk. BONK. Only two warriors came back, and one had no arm. Now everyone uses the long way and nobody talks about the shrine." He looks at the worm, then at the party. "Yark votes for the long way. Except there is no long way. Yark votes for QUIET."
location: Cragmaw Castle — back passage outside the owlbear's den (post-fight; owlbear wounded, retreated inside)

text:
It goes exactly like the plan. Mira's coin sails over the altar and chimes off the WEST wall — the grick whips around toward it, tentacles flaring, and pours itself at the sound. In the same breath, Relthus and Mira slip through the doorway and glide up the EAST wall, soft-footed on the rubble, Relthus's bow drawn and tracking the monster the whole way. It never turns. It is still nosing furiously through the west rubble for the phantom coin when the two of them step backward into the north corridor — through, past it, untouched, unheard.

So here is where everyone stands now: Relthus and Mira are in the north corridor — the last stretch, Yark says, before King Grol's tower. Behind them, across the shrine room and past the grick, Yark and Pearl wait at the south doorway, two small faces in the dark. The grick hunts the west wall between the two halves of the party.

Somewhere ahead, up the corridor: the tower. Gundren. The map. And perhaps an hour and a half of night left.
location: Cragmaw Castle — back passage outside the owlbear's den (post-fight; owlbear wounded, retreated inside)

text:
Relthus and Mira ghost up the north corridor, hugging the wall. It runs about sixty feet, then climbs a short flight of broad stone steps and ends at a heavy wooden door, iron-banded — the door to King Grol's tower.

One guard stands in front of it. A hobgoblin — the big, disciplined kind from the great hall — in real chainmail with a longsword and a shield, wide awake, eyes on the corridor. He has not seen you; you are still beyond the reach of his torch, and the shadows are deep. Fifty feet between you and him. No other guards. No other doors.

And Relthus's sharp ears catch what is happening on the OTHER side of that door. Three voices. First, a huge one, booming and angry — King Grol: "...map is worth MORE, elf. Grol knows what a MINE is." Second, a cold, smooth voice, patient the way ice is patient: "My master's offer is final. The gold, the map — and I take the DWARF as well." And third — a ragged, stubborn growl, a voice you have never heard, but a DWARF for certain, half-laughing through what sounds like a badly split lip: "Tell yer master... he can dig his own grave, then."

Gundren. Alive. On the other side of one door, one guard, and one bargain that is minutes from closing.
location: Cragmaw Castle — north corridor past the grick shrine (Relthus+Mira); Yark+Pearl at shrine's south doorway

text: Session 4 ends here — right at the door. Relthus and Mira crouch in the dark fifty feet from the last guard, with Gundren's voice on the other side of the stone and the deal about to close. Yark and Pearl hold their breath on the far side of the worm's shrine. One door. One guard. One bargain. Next session: LEVEL 3, and the door. Sleep well, heroes.

text: One hobgoblin guard stands in front of that door. He is tall, wearing chainmail, holding a longsword, and he looks bored — he keeps shifting his weight from foot to foot. He has not seen you. The corridor between you and him is straight and dark, with no other doors and a low stone bench along one wall.

text: Through the door you can hear three voices. Grol's deep growl: 'Gold first. Then the map. The dwarf costs extra.' A smooth, cold voice answering: 'You will have both prices before first light.' And a third voice — hoarse, stubborn, alive — Gundren's: 'You pox-ridden thieves couldn't read that map with three candles and a wish!' There is a THUMP, like a boot hitting someone, and then laughter. Gundren is still breathing, and still arguing. Relthus, Mira — what do you do?
location: Cragmaw Castle — north corridor past the grick shrine (Relthus+Mira); Yark+Pearl at shrine's south doorway

text: Relthus rises from the shadows, draws, and looses in one breath. The arrow crosses fifty feet of dark corridor and slams into the hobgoblin's shoulder, right above the edge of his chainmail. The guard staggers back against the iron-banded door — his sword clatters against the stone — and his mouth opens wide, sucking in air to scream. He is one heartbeat from raising the whole castle. Mira, you are faster than that heartbeat. What do you do?
